prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Scope: checked baggage from acceptance at bag-drop or transfer induction through screening, sorting, make-up and handoff for aircraft loading. The boundary includes airport conveyance, screening, routing, reconciliation, staging equipment and controls. It excludes airline loading beyond the outbound load control point. Objectives: safe screening, accurate bag-to-flight association, predictable throughput, timely delivery within departure cutoffs.

Actors: Baggage Operations Supervisor (oversees flow and recovery with the Security Duty Manager and Maintenance Technician). Explosives Response Team and Security Duty Manager (security response). Airline Ramp Coordinator (accepts staged bags). Staff confirm eligibility, verify passenger and flight, check size and weight, resolve held bags and confirm oversize routes and transfer tags.

Induction: Pier 4 Bag-Drop Unit (records accepted bag and initiates processing; sends the Oversize Exception Ticket when a bag exceeds the size envelope, receiver unstated; oversized bags are held until a route is approved). Bag Tag Printer (produces a durable uniquely identified tag per bag). Transfer Bag Feeder (identifies and records inbound transfer bags; sends the Late Transfer Bag Card, receiver unstated). Induction Tray Conveyor (controlled feed points; maintains separation between bags).

Control: Baggage Control System, alias Velvet (associates the tag ID with the passenger and flight record; checks the flight is open and the record complete; compares transfer data with routing before release). Concourse Zone Controller, alias Mosslight (local equipment; grants the induction permissive only when status and restrictions allow; produces the Recovery Route Card). Flight Data Gateway (supplies flight and routing records; sends the Flight Cutoff Advisory).

Screening: North and South Gate Scanners; Image Resolution Desk (operator image review); Secondary Inspection Chute.

Sorting and reconciliation: Primary Crossbelt Sorter (routes cleared bags to make-up). Bag Reconciliation Station.

Make-up and handoff: East and West Make-Up Conveyors; Carousel 7 Make-Up Unit (stages its departure); Outbound Load Control Desk (confirms readiness at handoff).

Requirements: bags with missing, unreadable or conflicting data are held before induction. Before induction, the record must be valid, the route available and the receiving equipment ready. Status, identity, routing and restrictions are exchanged via defined interfaces. No modes stated.

Document units:
S045: Interlocks stop feed movement when a jam, access-door opening, or loss of downstream readiness is detected.
S046: The North Gate Scanner reads the bag identifier as the bag enters the screening and sorting network.
S047: The North Gate Scanner is also known locally as Kestrel.
S048: The South Gate Scanner provides an independent read point for bags routed through its assigned entry path.
S049: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter receives inducted bags and directs them according to the active routing data.
S050: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter is also known locally as Juniper.
S051: When automated image review cannot resolve a bag image, staff at the Image Resolution Desk assess the available image and record a disposition.
S052: The Airline Ramp Coordinator sends a Carousel Release Slip when the outbound build is authorized.
S053: The Baggage Control System applies the approved screening profile to each bag using its tag data and the current operating configuration.
S054: The Induction Tray Conveyor presents bags to the screening equipment at a controlled spacing that supports reliable image capture.
S055: The Primary Crossbelt Sorter maintains bag identity and routes each bag according to the screening disposition available at the time of sorting.
S056: The North Gate Scanner and South Gate Scanner acquire screening images and return a disposition for each bag that passes through them.
S057: Screening equipment records image quality and alarm status so that an incomplete examination is not treated as a clear result.
S058: When automated image review cannot resolve a bag image, staff at the Image Resolution Desk assess the available image and record a disposition.
S059: The reviewer considers the full image, bag identification, and any system prompts before assigning a disposition.
S060: A bag remains under controlled routing while its image is awaiting review, and the system prevents it from entering an outbound make-up path prematurely.
S061: The South Gate Scanner produces a Manual Rescan Receipt when a manual rescan is required.
S062: A clear disposition permits normal routing only when the bag identity and screening record agree.
S063: An alarm, an unresolved image, or a missing screening record places the bag into an exception status for additional examination.
S064: The Baggage Control System routes exception-status bags to the Secondary Inspection Chute through a path that avoids normal outbound flows.
S065: The chute is monitored for occupancy so that a bag is not released into a blocked or unavailable inspection position.
